title: A fixed group versus each member: paired L-scope projections of two complete source paragraphs
phase: Exploratory reading development, not a fixed native test or reserved confirmation.
selection_note: Develop the specific L assertion version of45. Do not rerun203s already parked result-count comparison. No new parser, decoder or corpus census: manually align ten declared L occurrences in two already admitted complete paragraphs, retaining all residual text.
human_writer_hypothesis: A writer can describe the same named group as a whole or state a property of every member. The lexical predicate remains the same; the whole form signals its scope. This is a possible writing convention, not a recovered historical practice.

contract.group: The first complete raw paragraph group hypothetically introduces one nonempty participant set G. This is a positional role assumption, not a name translation or a known member list. Its entire spelling is retained; ksho is not split into k plus sho.
contract.context: One evaluation context kappa is held fixed throughout each paragraph. Neither group membership nor time/state changes silently at an unread group.
contract.predicates: For each CORE13 carrier X, one unassigned predicate P_X takes a nonempty participant set and kappa. The same P_X is used in both orientations and at every occurrence of this carrier.
contract.C: C_X := P_X(G,kappa), an assertion about G as a whole.
contract.D: D_X := for every g in G, P_X({g},kappa), an assertion about each member.
contract.C1: Exact Xol -> C_X; exact Xeol -> D_X.
contract.C1_reverse: Exact Xol -> D_X; exact Xeol -> C_X. Swap globally, never per target.
contract.arity: Both forms retain one group argument. No preceding or following written group is consumed as an extra operand.
contract.scope: Own-reader paragraph marks delimit the hypothesized scope. Within-paragraph line wraps and recorded drawing interruptions preserve G and kappa under an explicitly new unproved persistence assumption. This is not a repair of B3s immediate-neighbour contract.
contract.residuals: Every other written group remains visible and semantically unassigned. Holding G/kappa fixed across such groups is an assumption to be tested by a later full reading; unknown text is not declared meaningless.
contract.repetition: Repeated identical forms under fixed G/kappa repeat the same assertion. Preserve each textual occurrence. No new member, amount, event, product or intensity is inferred.
contract.inventory_limit: No initial-y deletion, no general e morpheme, no DY transfer. ysheol, qotchol, otchol, cphol and bare ol remain outside the declared L inventory.

semantic_corrections: IDEA203s proposed collective/distributive event or result distinction is not entailed by C_X versus D_X. A group event can have multiple results; several events can share a result. No outcome count may be inherited without an explicit separate contract.

evidence_account.motivation: 808/865 support context-dependent L variant behaviour beyond immediate neighbours;608 retains directed parts and extra whole-form information. These motivate trying a shared predicate with a whole-form scope change but do not identify that scope.
evidence_account.not_explained: C1 has no independently bound group sizes or members, no chosen P_X values and no observed selection rule predicting when the author chooses C or D. It does not explain915 phrase-ending coupling or reproduce manuscript word statistics.
evidence_account.previous_failures: B2 and B3 keep their documented failures.949 universal neighbour attachment,981 fixed state carry,916 new-pair nonconfirmation and1276 one-bit capacity exclusion are not repaired or rerun.
evidence_account.no_word_assignments: No oil, water, plant part, mixing, temperature, quantity, lexical name or concrete predicate value has been assigned.

profiles_reviewed.method: Existing vmanus-work words profile, exact standalone raw groups, all179 admitted selectors; no pooling readers or embedded strings. Counts below are ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b.

logical_selection_limit.singleton: For G={g}, C_X and D_X have identical truth conditions. Singleton compatibility cannot orient the spellings.
logical_selection_limit.positive_assertion_saturation: With all P_X unassigned and only positive L assertions, set P_X(S,kappa)=true for every nonempty S. Then both orientations satisfy every such projection, even for plural G. Internal consistency of this projection is therefore automatic and cannot select a scope interpretation.
logical_selection_limit.ceiling: This is a property of the incomplete C1 projection, not proof that a full reading is consistent, that the manuscript is meaningless, or that collective/distributive semantics is impossible.
logical_selection_limit.potential_difference: With a common bound G, predicate and context, an explicit P_X({a}) and explicit not-P_X({b}) for included members would contradict universal D_X. An omission is not negation and a later changed context is not the same case. A coherent provisional semantic grammar may supply such relations; they need not be independently confirmed before exploration.
logical_selection_limit.shared_relation_example: A uniformly defined contrary predicate Q with Q(S,kappa) -> not P(S,kappa) can provide a genuine contrast if the same reading binds b in G and Q({b},kappa). This is a source-free design example, not an assignment to any Voynich form. A larger G by itself does not remove the all-true countermodel.

spelling_rival: A meaning-preserving L spelling variant can retain separate written occurrences without scope differences. It remains unselected, as do both C1 orientations. Model permissiveness is not evidence in its favour.
decision: Retain this exact partial working construction, with both orientations and all66 residual groups. No complete reading or scope selection. Do not score more paragraphs merely for positive-assertion consistency or start a parser. Next construct one shared, nontrivial content relation that can distinguish a group assertion from a member assertion, using the same group and context in both readings; apply it only with an explicit source-text binding. A provisional relation is allowed without a confirmed seed. No relation is selected here. The f32v.10-11 product-reuse story has already been supplied in948 and must not be presented as new.
validation: Manual C1/C1_reverse applications by root and bounded_idea_supply; independent semantic/event-count audit by closure_error_audit and discriminating_test_review; exact reader sensitivity by cross_reading_opportunity. Source extraction preserves every raw group, separator, own paragraph flag and position; manual role counts are explicitly checked. No native model run or semantic validation claimed. false_closure_semantics independently confirms the all-positive saturation limit. Late predecessor-only addendum records948; the source alignment and ten manual assignments remain unchanged.
